chunks.rationale: Start with test/sidebar.test.tsx helpers (scopeTrigger, settledToggle, openCreateMenu) — every other file copies that selector contract. Then pinSnooze (pin block + two shelves + overflow data-pin-item) and multiSelect (flatVisibleThreadIds order: pinned, active, open shelves). Create/edit files (sidebarWorktreeCreate, sidebarIssue, orchestratorCreate, editProject) only swap header/scope selectors; ThreadCard files (prRender, sidebarFailedBadge, deliveryState) swap status-dot → data-status-label.
risks: Shelves default collapsed. A UI that ships default-open will fail the collapsed-header copy assertions (Snoozed (N) / Settled (N)) even if the toggles exist.

Create-item and issue-form selectors are queried without a projectId value. If the UI keeps data-create-worktree-thread="p1" that still matches; if it drops the attributes entirely the tests fail as intended.
SettledRow is still imported and mounted directly. If the UI worker unexports it, tsc fails — spec says keep the slim-row components.
data-settled-clear-all is not in the spec; clearSettled.test.tsx still pins it after opening the Settled shelf.
Runtime of npm run test:renderer is expected red until Sidebar.tsx lands. tsc --noEmit is the gate.

chunks.rationale: The written contract is .solenta/specs/t3-flat-sidebar.md (Deletions + selector lists). Tests were authored against that file, not against src/components/Sidebar.tsx (untouched, still the #567 Later-shelf implementation).
risks: Spec is silent on data-settle-all, data-settled-clear-all, localStorage boolean encoding, and whether create-item data attributes still carry the project id.
A parallel UI worker is rewriting Sidebar.tsx. Selector drift (data-slim-row missing, status label without data-failed flags, pin item text) will only show up when the branches merge.
Old #567 knowledge (partitionSidebar, Later · N) still describes the logic layer which remains exported; only the Sidebar render contract changed.
